newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey sells 125,000 T barley at tender - sources.
newsitem.headline: Turkey sells 125,000 T barley at tender - sources.

text.p: Turkey on Sunday sold 125,000 tonnes of feed barley for export in the second half of October at $136.07 per tonne, grain traders and other industry sources said.
The sale matched the top bid, placed by Glencore, in a public international export tender last Thursday, they said.
There was no immediate official confirmation.
Shipments are to be from Derince and Mersin ports in Panamax class vessels, according to the public bidding documents.
No malting barley was awarded, traders said.
Turkey had invited bids to export at least 200,000 tonnes of barley from domestic purchases made by the Turkish Grain Board (TMO) amounting to more than 600,000 tonnes.
Some traders said they were surprised by the relatively low volume finally awarded, but expected more barley to be exported later this year.

The TMO buys barley from farmers at prices some 25 percent above world markets and sells what it can abroad. But while the TMO needs export cash to finance its farm purchases, it may have been reluctant to widen its losses by exporting at too low a price, analysts said. Tender bids were as low as $121 a tonne.
